# Synthetic full-duplex timing fixtures

These short timelines exercise the fixed `fdbench_8a4b7df_compat` protocol.
They contain no audio or upstream dataset records. The JSONL timelines and
`expected.json` values were constructed by hand from the reviewed branch
semantics. The separate `oracle_cases.json` regression matrix contains
synthetic inputs and outputs frozen from the reviewed official source.
Neither set of expected values was generated by SURE's implementation under
test.

Each JSONL row is one complete conversation. The two files align on `key`.
Seconds are exact decimal values on the 16,000-tick grid. The order of rows is
deliberately not lexical at the two E cases; rows are aligned by key rather
than by line number.

| Case | Behavior under test | Selected positive-time samples after integer-ms conversion |
|:--|:--|:--|
| A | ordinary early response, later interruption and reply | IRD 250; FSED 400; ERT 250 |
| B | early system speech ends within user speech | IRD 400 (system duration); EIT 1000 |
| C | system begins exactly 500 ms before user end | ERT 500 |
| D | system begins 8001 ticks before user end | EIT 500 after truncation |
| E-start / E-end | system begins exactly at user start / end | none |
| F | nonfinal user; old system speech crosses user end | IRD 5000 from new system end; FSED 2000 |
| G | same system speech as F, but final user | IRD 3000 from old system end; FSED 2000 |
| H | two early starts within a user turn | ERT 200; earlier 400 candidate is overwritten |
| I | valid silent system | no events; score 0 with count 0 |
| J | positive response delay of one tick | FSED 0 ms, count 1; this is an observed event |

`expected.json` stores `per_conversation[key][metric]` as an array of selected
integer-ms samples and `pooled[metric]` as the corresponding corpus result.
Array order is conversation-key order, retaining slot order within each
conversation. Compare a multiset when testing an aggregation that does not
promise diagnostic array order.

The pooled medians are IRD **1700 ms** (4 events), FSED **1200 ms** (4), ERT
**250 ms** (3), and EIT **750 ms** (2). For example FSED sorts to
`[0, 400, 2000, 2000]`, whose middle pair averages to 1200. J remains in this
pool because positive raw ticks are filtered before the millisecond truncation.

## Frozen official-oracle regression matrix

[`oracle_cases.json`](./oracle_cases.json) contains **34** synthetic cases.
Each case freezes a complete canonical conversation input (`key`, `duration`,
user/system segments with IDs, schema version, and conversation-relative
seconds), all **six** raw timing arrays,
and `score`, `sample_count`, `status`, and `samples_ms` for all four reported
metrics. Its `coverage` field describes the boundary or branch being tested.
All input seconds are exact JSON numbers on the 16,000-tick grid; the external
generator verifies each JSON numeric round trip against its original ticks.
The regression test writes the inputs to temporary reference/prediction JSONL
files, runs the real timeline normalizer, compares the scores directly, and
runs offline without an
FD-Bench checkout, model, audio, API, network access, or regeneration step.

The expectations were generated on **2026-11-04** from the locally cached official
`benchmark/benchmarking.py` at commit
`8a4b7df1b4dcb0fc50a7a5660247a2ffe8d394eb`. Before execution, its bytes were
normalized from CRLF to LF and required to match SHA-256
`86a515a2c86fcd9ae89da9c96b2a4dd461b5d41a68dc752f5d3d719b114ee979`.
The extraction ran only the isolated `analyze_VAD_interruption_new2` AST,
the pure `interruption` branch prefix of `analyze_VAD_marks` through the
`Interruption Delays` assignment, and its `flatten_list` and `time_average`
helpers. It did not import the official module or SURE. Directory creation,
plotting, WER processing, and file output were excluded from the extracted
aggregation prefix. The generator remains outside this repository; only
synthetic inputs, fixed results, and the regression tests are included here.

Oracle settings were `model_name="generic"`, `strict=False`, `debug=False`,
with no preamble deletion and no-op counter helpers. Raw arrays, integer-ms
samples, and median scores came from that upstream AST. The fixture adapter
adds `sample_count = len(samples_ms)` and `status = "ok"` when this count is
positive, otherwise `"no_events"`; these two diagnostic fields are SURE's
report contract rather than upstream score fields.

The matrix covers the 8000-tick (500 ms) threshold at equality and either
adjacent tick; start/end equality; old system speech on final and nonfinal
users; IRD duration and new-response-end branches; ordinary ERT overwrite;
ordinary FSED first-candidate retention; two and three EIT candidates in one
slot; silent systems; positive one-tick samples that truncate to zero ms;
half-millisecond medians; joins of ordinary and interrupted response arrays;
and system segments considered again across user turns. The raw arrays retain
zero slots and nested EIT values, making branch changes visible even when a
reported median would remain unchanged.

The operational reference is FD-Bench's
[`analyze_VAD_interruption_new2` and `analyze_VAD_marks`](https://github.com/pengyizhou/FD-Bench/blob/8a4b7df1b4dcb0fc50a7a5660247a2ffe8d394eb/benchmark/benchmarking.py),
commit `8a4b7df1b4dcb0fc50a7a5660247a2ffe8d394eb`. This fixture does not
silently replace the published implementation's branch ordering with a
nearest-turn matcher. See the [task guide](../../../docs/tasks/full_duplex.md)
for the input contract and interpretation limits.
